# A transaction that names a basis for 40 USD and is then refused.
#
# The split below the sale states a cost that cannot be read. Every stated
# cost is parsed before the transaction is created — ahead of the pick, and
# ahead of any balance moving — so the refusal comes first and the basis is
# never touched.
#
# The second transaction is here because the CLI only saves a file when
# something was imported. Without it the refusal is the whole file, nothing is
# written, and the book on disk could not show a loss even if there were one.
#
# What this fixture produces: one error, one imported transaction, and both
# bases still reading their full 100.00 USD.
#
# Undoing a drawdown that has already happened is a different guarantee and is
# tested directly, in tests/unit/services/test_cost_basis_drawdown_is_reversible.py:
# no file can be refused between the drawdown and the end of the import, so a
# fixture claiming to reach that would assert nothing.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.
2026-01-01 open Expenses
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Misc
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

2026-03-01 * "Sell 40 USD beside a split whose cost cannot be read"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:USD -40.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.35"
		value: "-54.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{basis_a}"
	Assets:Bank:USD 10.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.35"
		value: "13.50"
		cost_basis_cost: "oops"
	Assets:Bank 40.50 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "40.50"

2026-03-02 * "An ordinary CAD transaction, so the import saves"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank -20.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "-20.00"
	Expenses:Misc 20.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "20.00"
